d: Why do Americans vote on a Tuesday? The answer goes back nearly 200 years, to a time when horses and carriages were the primary means of transport and most Americans lived in rural communities. In 1845, the US Congress established a common election date, choosing the Tuesday after the first Monday in November. But why Tuesday? Why November? And what did church days, farming schedules, market days and harvest seasons have to do with it? We trace the history behind America's unusual election-day tradition, examine why it continues today and explain how early voting and mail-in ballots have…
